about: The top of the instruments' tree (registry/README.md, "The tree"; the owner, 17 November 2026: "Maintain object-oriented principles in our instrument typology from higher levels (e.g., aerophones) all the way down to specific instrument instances"): what sounds, by E. M. von Hornbostel and C. Sachs's four classes ("Systematik der Musikinstrumente", Zeitschrift fuer Ethnologie 46 (1914), 553-590; no DOI), above every family the registry holds. A class writes what every instrument of it shares; a family, a type and an instance below it each only what is its own.

instrument.about: Any instrument a player plays: the root of the tree, what every family shares.

aerophone.about: An instrument whose air itself sounds (Hornbostel and Sachs's class 4): the winds, a column of air in a bore (objects/winds.json).

chordophone.about: An instrument whose stretched strings sound (Hornbostel and Sachs's class 3): the bowed strings (objects/bowed.json).

membranophone.about: An instrument whose stretched membrane sounds (Hornbostel and Sachs's class 2). The physical percussion's drums (docs/PHYSICAL_PERCUSSION.md) are not yet nodes below it.

idiophone.about: An instrument whose own body sounds (Hornbostel and Sachs's class 1). The physical percussion's bars and plates (docs/PHYSICAL_PERCUSSION.md) are not yet nodes below it.
